correctness.rationale: For any selected set with \(a\ge1\), domination is immediate from a selected clique vertex and the induced graph is exactly \(K_a\vee\overline{K_b}\). A perfect matching requires \(b\le a\) and even \(a+b\); these conditions are sufficient by matching every stable vertex to a distinct clique vertex and pairing the remaining even clique vertices. If \(a=0\), the only dominating candidate is the whole stable part, which is edgeless and has no perfect matching. Every larger paired-dominating set contains a matched edge, and every graph edge is itself paired-dominating, proving the minimal-set statement. The packaged checker exhaustively verifies all subsets for \(1\le r,n\le7\).

value.rationale: Complete split graphs are a canonical maximally joined subclass of split graphs, while paired domination is NP-complete on the full split-graph class. The result resolves the entire all-set structure on this natural boundary family, including a bivariate occupancy enumerator, all ordinary coefficients, exact minimum-set count, and the equality \(\Gamma_{pr}=\gamma_{pr}=2\). This is a structural classification on an infinite two-parameter graph family, not an arbitrary finite slice or a recomputation of a single scalar.
